question: Can I reach you at 2am?
html:
You can call at any hour. Right now we can't promise a live person will answer at 2am. This concept adds an AI voice agent so overnight calls get answered and booked instead of going to voicemail.

What happens at 2am

  • Today: We have no measured after-hours answer rate. Our model assumes about 35% of after-hours calls are lost (est.) (Voice AI research).
  • With the concept: An AI agent answers, logs the problem and books the first open slot. Urgent issues, like no heat in October, get flagged for the on-call technician.
  • Speed matters to you: A lead reached within 5 minutes is 21 times more likely to qualify than one reached at 30 minutes (Voice AI research). A fast answer means you get on the schedule sooner.

Why after-hours coverage counts

October is the busiest HVAC month nationally because of heating start-up (Punctual Pros demand model). Off-hours calls run 9.8% of HVAC inbound in October and peak at 14.1% in June. Most of them come between 5 and 9 pm local time (Punctual Pros demand model).

MeasureFigureSource
Home-services callers who reach a person52%Voice AI research
After-hours share of calls (model input)12% (est.)Voice AI research
After-hours calls lost (model input)35% (est.)Voice AI research
AI agent booking rate, vendor-reported70%; 90% with open capacityVoice AI research
Typical human booking rate42%Voice AI research

The AI booking rates are self-reported by the vendor and unaudited. Treat them as a range, not a promise (Voice AI research).

What we still need to know

  • Actual 2am call volume and answer rate. Pulling the call-tracking and dispatch history would show this.
  • How many overnight callers book elsewhere and how many call back in the morning. The model assumes 40% would have called back anyway (est.).

Every unanswered 2am call is a homeowner with an urgent problem who will try the next number. Closing the after-hours gap alone is worth about $390,000 a year in recovered jobs (est.) (Voice AI research).

Next actions

  1. Export 12 months of call logs by hour to replace the 12% and 35% assumptions with measured figures.
  2. Pilot an AI agent on overnight calls only, routing emergencies to the on-call technician.
  3. Compare booked jobs from the overnight pilot with the same weeks last year before expanding to daytime overflow.
  4. Price a self-built setup (about $0.12 a minute) against an off-the-shelf one ($1.67–$3 a call) (Voice AI research).
